note: THE CHECKER RECOVERS ABOUT A QUARTER OF THE CYNGHANEDD THAT IS THERE. Nothing was tuned; the shortfall is the finding. Three mechanical causes, each with a minimal repro. DEFECT 1, INTERNAL APOSTROPHE: units() strips only leading/trailing quotes, so the elisions Welsh uses constantly are out of inventory — units("a'i") is None, units("ai") is ['a','i']; units("sy'n") is None, units("syn") is ['s','y','n']. skeleton() then returns None and the WHOLE LINE is 'unreadable' before any rule runs. 31.0% of the Alun corpus contains one. DEFECT 2, PRINTED COMMAS READ AS CAESURAS: cynghanedd() splits on [,/|], so ordinary verse punctuation is taken for the gwant and a 3-comma line is forced down the sain path — 'Eto, Aled, atolwg' is REFUSED ('sain needs rhyme AND alliteration'), while 'Eto Aled | atolwg' returns croes on skeleton ['t']. DEFECT 3, THE GWANT IS PRINTED AS '--' AND '--' IS NOT IN THE SPLIT SET: this transcription does mark the englyn gwant, with a dash, e.g. 'Bryd a chorff yn ddiorffwys,--'; the comma split leaves a half of '--' whose words all strip to empty, so skeleton() returns None and the line is 'unreadable'. 14.6% of lines carry a '--'. note: AN ALLOGRAPH PAIR THAT fin.py READS AS TWO CONSONANTS. evidence: quality/phonology/cym.py normalise() folds em dash, en dash and figure dash to '--' and _marked_parts() then splits on it. Lines that split, per file: cywydd 6/108 (5.6%), Mynyddog 54/2758 (2.0%), Hwiangerddi 11/1408 (0.8%), Twm o'r Nant songs 1/759 (0.1%), Alun songs 0/216. Every instance inspected is punctuation. In the 1862 Pryse cywydd the dash comes in MATCHED PAIRS around an interjection -- 'Er pan rodded--trwydded trwch--' splits to ['Er pan rodded', 'trwydded trwch'], 'Ar fynydd--sathr Ofydd serch--' to ['Ar fynydd', 'sathr Ofydd serch'] -- so the second 'half' is the contents of a bracket. In Mynyddog it is a dialogue dash: 'William, William,--anwyl i mi.'
note: DOCTRINE 55, NEXT INSTANCE, AND IT NARROWS THE FIX RATHER THAN UNDOING IT. The comma was correctly demoted from caesura to punctuation; the dash was promoted to gwant in the same change, on the evidence of ONE edition (Gwaith Alun, where a trailing '--' really does mark the englyn gwant). Across five further Welsh files the dash is punctuation 72 times out of 72. The distinguishing feature is POSITION and PAIRING: a gwant is line-final or line-medial and SINGLE, an editorial dash is medial and usually PAIRED, and a paired dash makes the parenthetical content the answering half. Sharpest point: THE GWANT IS AN ENGLYN FEATURE AND A CYWYDD HAS NONE, so any caesura='marked' result on a cywydd file is by construction reading the typesetter. Nothing under quality/ was edited by this cell -- a sibling holds cym.py this round -- and the corpus headers say caesura='search' only
